en: To Rāghava, the mine of compassion, served by sages and worshipped by gods;
the sun to the lotus-face of Jānakī, a vessel of virtues;
who desires the welfare of Vāli’s son and is dear to Hanumān—the lotus-eyed one.
I bow to the elephant among the Raghus, who strikes terror into the *yātudhānas*. || 1 ||
The Lord who is the protector of Rāvaṇa’s younger brother, the bull among the Raghus whose blue sapphire-like gem adorns the breast of Maithilī,
and whose body awakens the lotus-faces of city women— He is my deity.
I bow to the elephant among the Raghavas, who increases the solar dynasty.
The subduer of enemies, whose stainless neck-region was adorned with golden earrings,
who was embellished by ornaments of gold and peacock-feathers,
and who was graced by beautiful anklets, necklaces, the Kaustubha gem, and ear-ornaments.
I bow to the elephant among the Raghavas, who increases the lineage of the Sun. || 3 ||
In the forest known as Daṇḍaka, he was the refuge for hosts of gods, siddhas, and yogis who delight therein;
he was intent on protecting the virtuous, praised by King Pārtha who possessed steadfastness,
and was highly skilled in severing the serpent-like arms of Kumbhakarṇa.
I bow to Rāghava, that elephant among men, who is affectionate toward his younger brother Lakṣmaṇa. || 4 ||
He who is beautifully adorned with garlands fragrant with *ketakī*, *karavīra*, and *jāti* flowers;
the bearer of glory (*Śrīdhara*) whose chest is reddened by the saffron from the breasts of the daughter of Mithilā;
the God of gods, the captivator of the hearts of all beings, and the Lord of the worlds.
I bow to the elephant among the Raghavas, who removes the fear of being reduced to slavery. || 5 ||

It was constantly and reverently worshipped day and night by twice-born brahmins who had mastered the Vedas and performed rites such as sacrifices, charity, meditative concentration, fire-offerings, and recitation;
it was the cause of Tāṭakā’s destruction and the slayer of her father and of Vālin.
I bow to Rāghava, that elephant among men, who protects his father’s command. || 6 ||
I take refuge in Hari,

the support of the universe, whose face is like a lotus, whose pair of feet are like lotuses, who is the infallible bringer of Rāvaṇa’s end, the effortless destroyer of the night-stalkers such as Khara and Dūṣaṇa, and the shelter for millions of hosts of monkey leaders.
I bow down to Rāghava, that elephant among men, who desires to perform the work of the gods.
He who was well-trained by Kauśika in the arts of weaponry, whose eyes were long, who possessed a beautiful smile, who was the protector of the helpless, who dwelt in all the worlds,
and who brought about the destruction of Rāvaṇa— the enemy of the gods led by Vāsava— and attained the supreme goal.
I bow to Rāghava, who is like an elephant and whose form resembles a dark blue cloud. || 8 ||
One should always recite with devotion this Rāghavāṣṭaka, which grants the fulfillment of desires, accomplishes refuge in the Imperishable One,
bestows the fruits of liberation and worldly enjoyment, and increases the attainment of wealth and grain;
it grants the compassionate glance of Ramacandra.
His mind was continuously offered at the pair of lotus feet of Rāmacandra. || 9 ||
O Rāma, Rāma, homage be to you; victory to Rāmabhadra, homage be to you! O Rāmacandra, homage be to you; victory to Rāghava, homage be to you!
O God of gods, homage be to you; victory to the King of Gods, homage be to you!
O Vāsudeva, let there be salutation unto you; victory to you, O king of heroes, let there be salutation unto you! || 10 ||
Thus ends the Śrī Rāghavāṣṭaka in its entirety.
